Hi, this game is probably one of the best I've ever played. It has a lot of cool references to different beliefs (Slavic / Nordic) and it is based on a very nice story that can move you sometimes. Of course, there are bugs in this game and some mechanics need to be fixed, but all of these things start to annoy you when you play the game again and you usually play with mods that fix it, so for me, the cons disappear... a bit. If you want to have the best experience with this game, I recommend read the books and playing the previous parts.

After seeing all the rave reviews for this game I felt that I needed to play it or I would be missing out. It is a competent game but it is about story first and game second. There is so much story and combat is too simplistic for me to get into. When I heard about the game I was really keen on learning about monsters and finding their weaknesses but after playing I learned that you just go to your "beastiary" screen and you are blatantly told three things that a monster is weak to. "wraiths are weak to anti-wraith potion and two other things for no reason" This kind of took out the mystery for me as I was hoping for something deeper.

If you are an action loving type who doesn't really care about cut scenes you may be bored by this game. I haven't played it much at this point (and I'm not sure if I'll play more) but so far it has been about 80% story exposition and 20% hacking up monsters. I can see how other people can like this but, personally, I prefer more slappy, less yappy.

I thought I was just jumping into another RPG. What I got is a living, breathing world that completely swallowed me whole.
The writing is incredible. Every quest — even the side quests — feels handcrafted, layered with emotion, mystery, or heartbreak. Some of the site quest lines alone could win an Emmy.
The characters arte deep, believable, and unforgettable. Whether you're talking to a stranger on the road or someone who’s been with you the whole journey, the emotional weight of these relationships sneaks up on you. You start to care — really care.
The world is immersive, rich, and full of soul. Every region feels distinct, from windswept coastlines to misty forests and bustling towns. It’s not just beautiful — it feels alive. You don’t just explore it — you exist in it.
The music still haunts me. The combat feels satisfying. And Gwent… I didn’t expect to become addicted to a card game inside another game, but here we are.
This game didn’t just entertain me — it made me feel like I lived in another world.
10/10. Slay a griffin. Play some Gwent. Make terrible romantic decisions. You won’t regret a second.

This game is a masterpiece, it's not perfect that's true but almost, I mean, yeah It has some bugs like bald Geralt, or the headshots hitbox but... Those are few little mistakes for a BIG game like this. In the other hand those awesome quests and challenging bosses are going to make you forget the bugs, the quests are so interesing not just the main but the contracts and the side quests, and if you bought the expansion pass those two are interesing as the base game itself. There's always something to do, getting some Gwent cards, killing some monsters, chilling around with some women or trying to find Ciri, I don't know how someone can get bored from playing this.

The art is beautiful, in general the game looks so good plus The witcher universe is fascinating so warning, If you like good RPGs and challenging combat be careful, this game is going to absorb your life, specially that new game + option when you're done but have some achievements missing.

Hope this was helpful and thanks CD projekt red for this amazing game, you guys have made many advances if we compare the other two games with this one. Great job, cyberpunk 2077 hype is real.

What can I say about The Witcher 3, I mean, other than it is probably the best game I have ever played?

Great story? Check.
Unforgettable characters? Check.
Great RPG? Check.
Immersive? Double Check.
Choices matter? Check.
Regret a few choices (and cry over them)? Check and check.
Soundtrack? Amazing. Check.
Side quests unrepetitive and interesting? Triple Check.

The only way I see that you might not enjoy this game, is if you don't care, at all, about story and simply just hate RPGs, other than that, it's a MUST HAVE title, and the full price is laughable considering the hours you can put in the game, the immersion of the world, it's polishment, and (limited, though present) replayability.

100/10 - Will start playing again.

A masterpiece of open world RPGs. The story is gripping from the first quest to the last, and even the small side quests have memorable characters and tough choices that actually matter. Velen, Skellige, and Novigrad feel alive, the combat is satisfying, and Geralt is one of gaming's best protagonists. Add in Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine, and you get well over 100 hours of top-tier content. Years later, it's still the benchmark. 10/10, would Toss a Coin again.

The Witcher 3 is one of those mammoth RPGs where a simple review cannot fully do it justice. There’s just so much to see and experience, with a story that will be very different from player to player, you have to experience it for yourself. Even then, to fully absorb everything the game has to offer, you’ll need to go through multiple play-throughs, making this a game that really could last months, or even years.

Mechanically, it doesn’t quite keep up with its ambitions, and the combat sluggishness, as well as an occasionally choppy frame rate and poorly designed menu do hamper it, but if you look past these problems, you’ll find one of the best RPGs, and a definite must-have title.

Brief review from someone initially excited for the new Remaster:

The facts - reloading a previous save after dying takes me at MINIMUM 30 seconds with an SSD. This coupled with the fact I am constantly dodging into invisible objects during combat in a Deathmarch campaign run makes this game, formerly a well established game with stable albeit dated combat, no longer enjoyable and ultimately unplayable. This remaster has also cost my system approximately 80 fps.

My opinion - the aforementioned fps drop, the environmental atmosphere and overall stability of The Witcher 3 were sacrificed for slightly improved textures that are only noticeable on youtube split screen comparison videos. A completely unnecessary and game breaking update for an upcoming DLC nobody asked for.
